image_description: The image displays the dorsal surface of a large crocodilian swimming in rippled water. Only the top of the head, the armored back, and the base of the tail are visible above the waterline. The skin texture appears rough and scaly with dark brown/grey coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout emerging from the water exhibits the characteristic tapered, V-shape distinct to crocodiles, rather than the U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject's mouth is closed and the jawline is submerged or obscured by the water angle; individual teeth and their interlocking nature cannot be visually verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eyes are clearly positioned on the very top of the skull (dorsal), allowing them to remain above water while the body is submerged, consistent with the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostril openings are visible at the anterior extremity of the snout, appearing as small dark spots on the dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the body shows a long, continuous structure covered in heavy, raised armor plating.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of rectangular, bony scutes run parallel along the spine, matching the anatomical description of Crocodylus niloticus.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of dark earthy tones, and the texture appears rugged and non-reflective compared to the surrounding water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral (belly) side is completely submerged and not visible in this dorsal-view shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are tucked against the body or submerged beneath the water surface; no digits or webbing are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior section of the animal shows a thick, muscular transition into the tail, which appears laterally flattened as it trails in the water.

alignment_reasoning: The image demonstrates high fidelity to the 'African crocodile' class. All testable checkpoints regarding head shape, eye placement, nostril position, and dorsal scute arrangement are present and accurate. Several checkpoints were correctly marked untestable due to occlusion by water (teeth, belly, limbs), which is physically consistent with a swimming animal. No structural deviations were found in the visible anatomy.
artifact_reasoning: No AI-generation artifacts were detected. The water ripples interact naturally with the subject's body (no edge bleeding or floating effects). The texture of the scutes is consistent and detailed without melting or pattern repetition errors. Lighting and shadows are physically plausible.
